claims.text: In bioinspired high-entropy alloys, retention of toughness is primarily governed by the connectivity of an embedded ductile phase.
A continuously connected ductile-phase network promotes localized plastic deformation through nanoscale shear-band formation.
Localized plastic deformation in the ductile phase dissipates fracture energy.
The connected ductile phase bridges cracks through unfractured ligaments.
The connected ductile phase deflects crack paths.
Disrupting ductile-phase connectivity reduces crack bridging and crack deflection.
Disrupting ductile-phase connectivity produces more brittle failure.
Disrupting ductile-phase connectivity causes a measurable decrease in fracture toughness.
The proposed initial material contains a hard matrix.
The proposed initial material contains an intentionally engineered, contiguous network of a ductile phase.
Ductile-phase volume fraction and connectivity can be varied through minor compositional changes or processing while overall composition remains nearly constant.
Samples with a well-connected ductile-phase network will have higher fracture toughness than samples with a disrupted or less-connected network.
Samples with a well-connected ductile-phase network will retain strength better than the optimized-connectivity baseline.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold from room temperature to the relevant service limit under controlled strain rates.
The mechanism may not apply to homogeneous or non-networked microstructures or to systems lacking a soft phase.
The cited HEC/Cr7C3 ceramic has a contiguous Cr7C3 plastic-phase network within a predominant hard high-entropy-carbide phase.
In the cited HEC/Cr7C3 ceramic, Cr7C3 accommodates approximately 30.8% compressive engineering strain by forming multiple nanoscale shear bands.
The quantitative relationship between ductile-phase connectivity and toughness retention has not yet been established.
Direct quantitative evidence for this connectivity mechanism in high-entropy alloys is still emerging.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says a well-connected network will show better strength retention than a baseline that is itself defined as having optimized, contiguous connectivity. No distinction is provided that would allow the test group to exceed an already optimized-connectivity baseline.
